bug_semantics: ZPan v1's Token constructor globally initialized jwtutil with the literal HMAC signing secret "123". The same utility issued and verified RoleClaims containing attacker-relevant Subject and Roles fields, and LoginAuth trusted a verified z-token cookie for identity and RBAC. Anyone knowing the repository value could therefore sign an HS512 token claiming an arbitrary uid and the admin role and remotely reach administrator-only APIs; issue #219 demonstrates GET /api/system/options/core.email with a forged admin cookie.
flaw_origin: Commit 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 (saltbo, 2021-02-01, 'refactor: remove the moreu depend && add user supports') is the smallest true first-writer. It created internal/app/service/token.go with NewToken calling jwtutil.Init("123"), plus the new user-token and LoginAuth flow that consumed it. This was not a move of the vulnerable line: its sole parent 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c has no internal/app/service/token.go and no jwtutil.Init call.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object check only: `git cat-file -p 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5` records author and committer `saltbo <saltbo@foxmail.com>`, one parent, a GPG signature, and only the subject `refactor: remove the moreu depend && add user supports`; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity. The Claude Co-Authored-By trailer on later v2 reset/deletion commit b817cab2c1627d9cadc2239492d9b5c16afc1c59 is not on the BIC and is excluded.
evidence: In the assigned clone, `git log -L '/func NewToken/',+4:internal/app/service/token.go 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947^` resolves the complete vulnerable constructor to 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 and shows its /dev/null-to-file hunk containing `jwtutil.Init("123")`; `git log --all -S'jwtutil.Init("123")' -- internal/app/service/token.go` independently shows the lifecycle as the 4fae6e2 addition, b817cab2 deletion during the v2 repository reset, and 8662db8 replacement. Direct parent verification is reproducible with `git cat-file -e 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c:internal/app/service/token.go` (fatal: path does not exist) and `git grep -n -F 'jwtutil.Init' 3de132e2248fa8257f5e0dc2aa688bff8f94418c -- '*.go'` (no match). At v1.6.5, internal/app/service/token.go initializes `123`, service/user.go uses that Token for issue/verify, internal/pkg/authed/authed.go reads cookie `z-token`, internal/pkg/middleware/auth.go verifies it and trusts its Subject/Roles, and auth_rbac.yml restricts `/api/system/options/core.email` to admin. First-party issue https://github.com/saltbo/zpan/issues/219 identifies HS512, supplies a forged admin z-token, and demonstrates that endpoint. Tag checks with `git grep -n -F 'jwtutil.Init("123")' <tag> -- '*.go'` find no match in v1.4.1, but find the line in v1.5.0, v1.6.5, and v1.7.0-beta2; thus the repository's first vulnerable release is v1.5.0, the last v1.6 release before the patch is v1.6.5, and the historical beta2 tag also carries the flaw. `git show 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947 -- internal/app/service/token.go cmd/root.go` directly replaces `jwtutil.Init("123")` with `jwtutil.Init(JWTSecret())`, generates a random 32-byte per-installation `security.jwt_secret`, persists it for installs/upgrades, and rejects missing installed configuration. The fix is a one-parent commit whose parent is exactly v1.6.5 commit 33eec01e971f206356c76df79c4148e3f8d1752f; lightweight tag v1.6.6 resolves exactly to 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947. PR #410 and the v1.6.6 release both identify that commit/release as the direct patch and recommend v2 for the retired v1 line.
reasoning: The vulnerable constant and its security-relevant consumer path first appear together in 4fae6e2, while the immediate parent lacks both the file and the initialization; the refactor wording therefore does not make this line a carrier or move. The later JWT-package update 29589509b3e0f178574c2bf3a9a39fe13da52f8e leaves the hardcoded secret intact, and the AI-marked b817cab2 commit merely deletes the v1 tree during the later v2 reset. Commit 8662db8 is the direct causal closure on the v1.6.5 parent and is released as v1.6.6. Because the only admissible authorship evidence is the 4fae6e2 commit object and that object identifies a human author/committer with no AI attribution or bot marker, the vulnerability is NOT_AI.
